purpose: P0-S2 evidence batch 2a: HU-study, HU-work, LU-study, LT-study, LT-work.

records.claim: Third-country nationals wishing to study in Hungary must obtain a residence permit for study purposes. Applicants must hold a valid acceptance letter from a Hungarian higher-education institution, demonstrate sufficient financial means, and satisfy the general conditions for entry and residence under Hungarian immigration law.
records.methodology: Direct review of current NDGAP factsheet for residence permit for the purpose of studies.

records.claim: Hungary requires study-permit applicants to demonstrate sufficient financial means to cover their stay. The applicable subsistence reference is set by Hungarian law and must cover accommodation and living costs for the duration of the permit; applicants must show they can support themselves without recourse to public funds.
records.methodology: Direct review of current NDGAP factsheet financial-means requirements for study residence permits.

records.claim: Applications for a Hungarian study residence permit are submitted to the competent regional directorate of the National Directorate-General for Aliens Policing. Applicants already in Hungary apply in person; those outside Hungary apply at the Hungarian consulate in their country of residence. The permit is issued for the duration of the study programme and must be renewed annually.
records.methodology: Direct review of current NDGAP factsheet application process for study residence permits.

records.claim: Third-country nationals seeking employment in Hungary must obtain a residence permit for employment purposes. The applicant must have a valid job offer from a Hungarian employer, and the employer must demonstrate that the position could not be filled by a Hungarian or EU/EEA national, subject to the applicable labour-market test and quota rules.
records.methodology: Direct review of current NDGAP factsheet for residence permit for the purpose of employment.

records.claim: Hungary's employment residence permit requires the applicant to receive remuneration at least equal to the applicable statutory minimum wage or the sector-specific minimum for the role. The employer's job offer must specify the salary, which must comply with Hungarian labour law requirements.
records.methodology: Direct review of current NDGAP factsheet financial requirements for employment residence permits.

records.claim: Applications for a Hungarian employment residence permit are submitted to the competent regional directorate of the National Directorate-General for Aliens Policing or at the Hungarian consulate abroad. The employer initiates the labour-market availability check; once cleared, the applicant submits the residence permit application with the job offer and supporting documents.
records.methodology: Direct review of current NDGAP factsheet application process for employment residence permits.

records.claim: Third-country nationals wishing to study in Luxembourg must obtain a temporary authorisation to stay for study purposes. Applicants must be enrolled or accepted at a recognised Luxembourg educational institution, be at least 18 years old, hold a valid travel document, and demonstrate sufficient financial resources and health insurance.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Guichet.lu student immigration guidance for third-country nationals.

records.claim: Luxembourg requires student applicants to demonstrate financial resources sufficient to cover living costs and tuition for the duration of their studies. The applicable reference amount is linked to the Luxembourg social minimum wage; applicants must show they can support themselves without recourse to public funds.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Guichet.lu financial-means requirements for student immigration.

records.claim: Luxembourg student immigration applications are submitted to the Immigration Directorate of the Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs. Applicants outside Luxembourg apply at the Luxembourg consulate in their country of residence. The temporary authorisation to stay is issued for one academic year and must be renewed annually with proof of academic progress.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Guichet.lu application process for student immigration.

records.claim: Third-country nationals wishing to study in Lithuania must obtain a temporary residence permit for studies. Applicants must hold a valid acceptance letter from a Lithuanian higher-education institution, demonstrate sufficient financial means, hold valid health insurance, and satisfy the general conditions for entry and residence under Lithuanian immigration law.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Migration Department of Lithuania guidance for temporary residence permit for studies.

records.claim: Lithuania requires study-permit applicants to demonstrate financial means sufficient to cover living costs and tuition. The applicable subsistence threshold is set by Lithuanian law and must be demonstrated for the full duration of the permit period; applicants must show they can support themselves without recourse to public funds.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Migration Department of Lithuania financial-means requirements for study permits.

records.claim: Applications for a Lithuanian study temporary residence permit are submitted to the Migration Department. Applicants outside Lithuania apply at the Lithuanian consulate in their country of residence for a national visa, then apply for the residence permit after arrival. The permit is issued for up to one year and must be renewed annually.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Migration Department of Lithuania application process for study permits.

records.claim: Third-country nationals seeking employment in Lithuania must obtain a temporary residence permit for work. The applicant must have a valid employment contract or job offer from a Lithuanian employer. Certain occupations and high-skilled roles may be exempt from the labour-market test under the EU Blue Card or national high-skilled worker provisions.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Migration Department of Lithuania guidance for temporary residence permit for work.

records.claim: Lithuania's work residence permit requires the applicant to receive remuneration at least equal to the applicable Lithuanian average monthly gross wage threshold for the relevant permit category. The salary must be specified in the employment contract and comply with Lithuanian labour law.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Migration Department of Lithuania financial requirements for work permits.

records.claim: Applications for a Lithuanian work temporary residence permit are submitted to the Migration Department. Applicants outside Lithuania apply at the Lithuanian consulate for a national visa, then apply for the residence permit after arrival or the employer may initiate the process. The permit is tied to the specific employer and role and must be renewed if employment changes.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Migration Department of Lithuania application process for work permits.
